usage: hyp <command> [flags]

Every write command needs --why and an actor (--actor or $HYP_ACTOR).
Statuses are derived from events; no command can set one.

setup:
  init                                   create .tree in the current directory
  version                                print the hyp version

write:
  add goal --title T [--body B] [--alias A] [--line L]... [--cite N=KEY]...
  add dq   --parent REF --title T [--body B] [--alias A]
  add hyp  --parent REF --title T [--body B] [--alias A] [--subject PATH]...
  add exp  --parent REF --title T --recipe NAME@V|none [--rubric NAME@V|reading] [--records PATH]... [--target REF|none]... [--alias A]
  record   --exp REF [--verdict REF=supports|contradicts|inconclusive]... --observation O [--evidence P]... [--limit L]... [--closes R#N]...
  retract REF | abandon REF | reaffirm REF
  supersede NEW --old OLD
  amend HYP --body B                     revise a Hypothesis body
  subject HYP [PATH...] [--base C]       tie a Hypothesis to the base and files that embody its claim
  link FROM depends_on|external_ref TO   unlink FROM TYPE TO
  select DQ [HYP]                        admitted only when hyp status owes it (no HYP: print the suggestion only)
  unselect DQ | defer DQ | withdraw DQ|EXP | resume DQ
  checkpoint [--summary S] [--goal G] [--refers K[=TEXT]]...   the runner's report: a summary, refers, or both
  answer [--answer R#rN=TEXT]... [--accept K=TEXT]... [--returns K=TEXT]...   the owner's act; no --why

read (REF/TIME: an event id, a node ref, or an RFC3339 time):
  status [--as-of REF|TIME] [--max-lines N] [--live]   orientation screen, 60 lines by default; --live hides contradicted rivals
  show REF|R-id#n|G-id#n [--as-of REF|TIME]  one node, or one limit or line, in full, with its history
  diff --since REF|TIME                       status changes and events since a point
  render --markdown [--as-of REF|TIME]        the whole tree as Markdown, untruncated
  check                                       rejected events, bad lines, warnings
  signals [--json]                            design marks for the whole tree: one-rival, D1
  events --json                               applied events in merge order, and rejected ones, as JSON for scripts
  prompt G-id --actor A [--branch B] [--pr N] [--experiments N]   the /goal prompt for a Goal, from its body's constraints block

bundle (a recipe in recipes/ or a rubric in rubrics/; a name lives in one library):
  bundle hash DIR [--json]               the bundle hash add exp --recipe or --rubric records for DIR
  bundle check                           every pin to a versioned bundle, in every tree under the repo root, still matches it
  bundle new NAME@1 [--rubric]           write a first recipe, or with --rubric a first rubric, beside the nearest .tree/ from hyp's template; fill every hyp:placeholder
  bundle new NAME@N --from NAME@M        copy bundle NAME@M to the next version NAME@N in its library, writing from:

3:The words hyp uses for its tree, its recipes and its sandboxes. The specs ([replay-spec.md](replay-spec.md), [sandbox-spec.md](sandbox-spec.md)) and the recipe format define the rules; this file only fixes which word means what, links the rule's section instead of restating it, and names the Go type that owns each concept where one exists. It also names the two scopes of this repository, core and self-review, and the test that puts an item in one; [core-and-self-review.md](core-and-self-review.md) maps the repository onto them.
30:Everything replay derives from a store's events: each node, a derived record per node kind (Hypothesis, Question, Experiment and Result) with its own status word, the Goal's state, rejections, limits and selections ([spec §8](replay-spec.md#8-projection-what-replay-returns)). Nothing stores it; every read replays (ADR 0006). In code: `replay.Projection`.
34:The root node of a tree, `G-`: what the investigation is for. A store holds many Goals, and a tree is the view of one Goal and every node whose parents lead to it (ADR 0020); each Goal has its own lines, OWED and coverage. A Goal is complete when every live DesignQuestion under it is answered ([spec §7.5](replay-spec.md#75-goal)). Its lines are the limits the owner records on it (see Line); the owner's "met" is a complete Goal with no line under OWED, read from `hyp status`, and hyp stores no word for it. No one changes a Goal once it is written: its lines come with its add, and a new purpose is a new Goal, which may sit in the same store and cite the keys it carries over (see Line). By what its candidate is, a Goal is a discovery Goal or a build Goal; hyp stores no kind, and the same events, rules and ledger serve both (ADR 0020).
46:A Goal whose candidate is a commit: building is a Goal like any other. A line asserts one property of the candidate, decided by its own tests or one pinned instrument: `[P]` pins what a valid input produces, and `[N]` pins that a forbidden state is refused. Each commit is a Hypothesis whose subject is the base plus that commit's change, and a fix is a new Hypothesis that supersedes it. Each Experiment's verdict rule asks for red on base and green on the candidate; the base of the red run's subject is where the build starts, and the Goal records no start commit. A finding of a run's review that is a case of a line is a limit; one that is not is an out-of-Goal finding. A change to a skill is a build Goal too (ADR 0021).
65:The section of `hyp status` that names the one step due from the owner on each question the Frontier prints: `choose: H…, H…` when they should choose between the candidates and the runner owes nothing on the question. A question the Frontier does not print asks nothing, and the choice is owed again once it prints. It also lists every open reading, which blocks nothing, and every referred limit on a candidate. `hyp status G-…` lists one Goal's items; in a store with many Goals, `hyp status` prints one Awaiting owner list, grouped by Goal.
76:**Open limits**:
77:The section of `hyp status` that lists every open limit, whatever the state of its question and whether the Frontier prints it. It is a list, not open work: the open work in it is what Owed and Awaiting owner name.
80:Another Hypothesis under the same DesignQuestion. Two live rivals are **separated** when a non-retracted Result gives them different verdicts, and `hyp show Q` lists the pairs that are not; exhaustiveness is a property of the cases run on the candidates (see Limit), never of the set of rivals, which the owner may reserve. A live rival is live and not contradicted ([spec §7.1](replay-spec.md#71-hypothesis-status-first-matching-rule-wins)); the one-rival refusal and the one-rival and D1 signals read the live rivals of an Experiment's parent at its add ([spec §8](replay-spec.md#8-projection-what-replay-returns), Rivals at add).
96:A node, `R-`, under an Experiment, that records what a run observed: a verdict per target of its Experiment, an observation, evidence pointers and any limits ([spec §4](replay-spec.md#4-event-types-closed-set)). It is recorded or retracted, and a retracted Result no longer counts. In code: `replay.Res`, which holds its status, pins, questionable flag and uncontained reasons, in `Projection.Results`.
144:Retired by ADR 0019. It was the `confirm` event in which a role judged a select `sufficient` or `insufficient`; the last use was the owner's confirm of a scope-change select. `hyp confirm` exits 2. An old owner confirm replays only the limits it accepted ([spec §4](replay-spec.md#4-event-types-closed-set)), and an old verifier confirm applies nothing. The owner still "confirms" in plain speech when they choose or accept.
145:_Avoid_: approve, review; verdict (alone: a confirm's answer was a confirm verdict)
155:Retired by ADR 0015. It was the role that confirmed every select, independently of the actor who made it. Old verifier confirms replay as history and apply nothing, and `hyp confirm` is retired (ADR 0019). Any actor may still review: a defect is recorded as a Result, a retract or a limit. In code: `event.RoleVerifier`, read only from old logs.
156:_Avoid_: reviewer, checker (as a role)
159:The person hyp asks to act on real choices, and the role they act in. The owner adds the Goal with its lines, and then answers what the ledger lists under Awaiting owner: a reading or a referred limit with an Answer, and a choice between candidates (`choose:`). Whoever runs the tree records a choice as the select, with the owner's words in `--why`; the tree holds what was chosen, but not who chose it ([ADR 0015](adr/0015-the-select-is-the-gate.md)). hyp does not authenticate actors, so an owner act records that someone wrote an answer; that the owner stood behind it rests on the procedure. The owner's role and what they never do are stated in [principles.md](principles.md#7-who-does-what), and the moves in [spec §8.2](replay-spec.md#82-keyed-items-limits-lines-and-readings). In code: `event.Answer`; `event.RoleOwner` on old owner checkpoints.
163:The owner's act, its own event type (ADR 0020): `answers` for readings, `accepts` and `returns` for referred limits, each item a key with the owner's words for it, and at least one key. It has no node, no summary, no why and no role, and owner and runner fields never mix in one event. One answer may settle keys of several Goals. An item in `answers` is a first answer of an open reading or a revision of an answered one, derived from the reading's state. An accept means only that this Goal does not run the case. `hyp answer` writes it; an old owner checkpoint's `closes`, `revises`, `accepts` and `returns` are read-only history that replay still applies ([spec §4](replay-spec.md#4-event-types-closed-set)). In code: `event.Answer`.
167:The runner's report on one Goal: a `summary` of where the work stands, `refers` that hand limits to the owner with why, or both, and a required `why`; an empty one is refused. `hyp status` prints its Goal's last one, never an old owner checkpoint, and a run records one at each stop. It holds no owner act: an old owner checkpoint's `role`, `closes`, `revises`, `accepts`, `returns` and `lines` are read-only history that replay applies and no command writes (owner decision of 2026-11-11). In code: `event.Checkpoint`.
170:**Limit**:
171:A case the Goal covers that no check has yet run on a Hypothesis. It is a keyed item with two births and one life: a Result records a limit its run left uncovered, keyed `<result-id>#<n>` (ADR 0016), and the owner records a line of the Goal, keyed `G-<goal-id>#<n>` (see Line). Its one job is to name the next case to run: an Experiment aims at it (`--aims`), and a later Result that runs the case on the candidates closes it (`--closes`), so its verdicts separate the rivals. A runner refers a limit that no test within the Goal can close, or whose case is void for every candidate (`hyp checkpoint --refers K=WHY`), which moves it from the runner's Owed items to Awaiting owner. The owner answers the refer with an Answer: accepts it (`hyp answer --accept K=TEXT`), so this Goal does not run the case and a later Goal may carry it by citing the key, or returns it (`--returns K=TEXT`) when the Goal covers its case, which makes it the runner's again; a return also reopens an accepted limit, and an accept needs a refer first. One move table states each move, from which state and by whom ([spec §8.2](replay-spec.md#82-keyed-items-limits-lines-and-readings)). A close records that the case ran, whatever the verdicts, and a limit's category is never stored: it is what its closers' verdicts, an accept, and the latest refer or return say. A limit's hand (the latest refer, return or accept) and its closers are two facts, and an **open** limit is one neither closed nor accepted; open is said of a Result's limit only. An open limit is owed while its question has a candidate, whichever Hypotheses its Result judged, so the select waits on it ([spec §8](replay-spec.md#8-projection-what-replay-returns), Limits). Other notes a run makes have homes of their own: the scope of a run goes in the Experiment body, a procedure note or a commit goes in the observation with the commit in a cited file, and a premise is a `depends_on` edge. In code: `replay.Limit`.
175:A limit the owner records on the Goal: a case every candidate must meet, keyed `G-<goal-id>#<n>`. A Goal's lines come with its add (`hyp add goal --line TEXT`), and no later event adds one (ADR 0020); an old Goal's lines, written on its first owner checkpoint, keep their keys. A line may cite 0 to 10 keys settled when it is written (`--cite N=KEY`): a line, an accepted or closed limit, an answered reading, or a selected or contradicted Hypothesis. What a cite means (carried, forbidden, applied or realised) is derived from the key's state at the line's place in the log, and a later change is only a `hyp check` warning. A line is never edited: what it means is a reading and the owner's answer; a line the Goal no longer needs is referred by the runner and accepted by the owner; a case under a line is a limit, returned by the owner when the Goal covers it; a new line or a new purpose is a new Goal, which may sit in the same store. A line is neither open nor closed: `hyp status` prints its hand when it has one, `covered on Q-…` or `uncovered on Q-…: H-…` for each top-level question with a candidate (see Coverage), and the Results that ran it. A line is owed as a `limit` item on each live top-level question of its own Goal where it is uncovered, and holds that question's select. A verdict is per Hypothesis, never per line: a Result that closes several lines and contradicts a Hypothesis says the cases ran and the Hypothesis failed, not which line, and its observation says which check failed. `hyp status` prints the lines under LINES, and `hyp show G-…#n` prints one ([spec §8](replay-spec.md#8-projection-what-replay-returns), Lines). In code: a `replay.Limit` whose `Question` is empty, and its `Cites`.
179:A finding, often from a run's review, that is a case of none of the Goal's lines and asks no question about what a line means. It is not a limit, since a limit is a case the Goal covers, so it gets no tree event, no refer and no accept, and it never holds the select. The runner names it in its stop checkpoint's summary and its last message as a possible new Goal or issue, and the owner decides at global scope whether to add one. A defect in text the run changed and may edit is not one: the run fixes it with a commit.
180:_Avoid_: limit, refer (for a case no line covers), side note
183:An item created as one entry inside its parent's event and addressed as `<parent>#<n>` or `<parent>#r<n>`: a limit or a reading inside a Result, or a line of the Goal. Its text is fixed, it takes no edge, and it is gone when its Result is retracted. Only other events move its state, and one move table per kind says which move applies from which state and by whom ([spec §8.2](replay-spec.md#82-keyed-items-limits-lines-and-readings)). It is not a node: it has no add event, no title and no status of its own. In code: `internal/replay/keyed.go`.
191:The ledger `hyp status` prints under OWED: each item of open work on a question and who owes it, the runner; the owner's items print under Awaiting owner ([spec §8.1](replay-spec.md#81-ledger-what-the-tree-owes)). OWED is per Goal: `hyp status G-…` prints one Goal's, and in a store with many Goals `hyp status` prints a GOALS table with what each Goal's runner owes. A line of the Goal is owed on each live top-level question that has a candidate no closer covers, as a `limit` item keyed `G-…#n`. A move never crosses Goals: only an item's own Goal refers, aims at, closes or applies it. An answered question owes only its limit, reading, referred and premise items. It is derived, never stored, and owing an item changes no status; `hyp select` reads it to admit a select. When the runner owes nothing, OWED ends with `runner owes nothing: stop and report to the owner`, the stop a run reads. In code: `replay.Projection.Owed`.
195:Where a question's decision stands, derived by one rule, first match wins, and never stored ([spec §8.1](replay-spec.md#81-ledger-what-the-tree-owes)): **closed** (answered, deferred or withdrawn; a select that stands is an answered question), **waits** (on runner work, an open reading with a reach, a referred limit, a premise, or a sub-question, in that order), **no candidate**, or **owed** (the runner's select of a lone candidate, or the owner's choice). The ledger owes a select or a choice only on an owed turn; `hyp select` refuses with the first thing the turn waits on; `hyp status` prints a `waits on …` line for each thing other than runner work. In code: `replay.Turn`, from `Projection.Turn`.
211:A limit or answered reading an Experiment is planned to settle, named with `hyp add exp --aims`. An aim is intent: it moves the item to `in_progress`, and to `aimed_not_settled` when every aiming Experiment has a Result and none closed or applied it. Only a Result's `--closes` or `--applies` settles the item, and settling it never answers a question.
438:Every concept hyp has, and everything a user who installs hyp into another repository runs, loads or reads there. A concept stays core when self-review is what tests it.
441:**Self-review**:
442:The recipes this repository keeps to test hyp, whatever repository the runner works on, with the inputs only they use. Investigating hyp is an activity, not a scope: a tree about hyp takes the scope of its question, and a tree about another project is a self-review input.

3:The words hyp uses for its tree, its recipes and its sandboxes. The specs ([replay-spec.md](replay-spec.md), [sandbox-spec.md](sandbox-spec.md)) and the recipe format define the rules; this file only fixes which word means what, links the rule's section instead of restating it, and names the Go type that owns each concept where one exists. It also names the two scopes of this repository, core and self-review, and the test that puts an item in one; [core-and-self-review.md](core-and-self-review.md) maps the repository onto them.
30:Everything replay derives from a store's events: each node, a derived record per node kind (Hypothesis, Question, Experiment and Result) with its own status word, the Goal's state, rejections, limits and selections ([spec §8](replay-spec.md#8-projection-what-replay-returns)). Nothing stores it; every read replays (ADR 0006). In code: `replay.Projection`.
34:The root node of a tree, `G-`: what the investigation is for. A store holds many Goals, and a tree is the view of one Goal and every node whose parents lead to it (ADR 0020); each Goal has its own lines, OWED and coverage. A Goal is complete when every live DesignQuestion under it is answered ([spec §7.5](replay-spec.md#75-goal)). Its lines are the limits the owner records on it (see Line); the owner's "met" is a complete Goal with no line under OWED, read from `hyp status`, and hyp stores no word for it. No one changes a Goal once it is written: its lines come with its add, and a new purpose is a new Goal, which may sit in the same store and cite the keys it carries over (see Line). By what its candidate is, a Goal is a discovery Goal or a build Goal; hyp stores no kind, and the same events, rules and ledger serve both (ADR 0020).
46:A Goal whose candidate is a commit: building is a Goal like any other. A line asserts one property of the candidate, decided by its own tests or one pinned instrument: `[P]` pins what a valid input produces, and `[N]` pins that a forbidden state is refused. Each commit is a Hypothesis whose subject is the base plus that commit's change, and a fix is a new Hypothesis that supersedes it. Each Experiment's verdict rule asks for red on base and green on the candidate; the base of the red run's subject is where the build starts, and the Goal records no start commit. A finding of a run's review that is a case of a line is a limit; one that is not is an out-of-Goal finding. A change to a skill is a build Goal too (ADR 0021).
65:The section of `hyp status` that names the one step due from the owner on each question the Frontier prints: `choose: H…, H…` when they should choose between the candidates and the runner owes nothing on the question. A question the Frontier does not print asks nothing, and the choice is owed again once it prints. It also lists every open reading, which blocks nothing, and every referred limit on a candidate. `hyp status G-…` lists one Goal's items; in a store with many Goals, `hyp status` prints one Awaiting owner list, grouped by Goal.
76:**Open limits**:
77:The section of `hyp status` that lists every open limit, whatever the state of its question and whether the Frontier prints it. It is a list, not open work: the open work in it is what Owed and Awaiting owner name.
80:Another Hypothesis under the same DesignQuestion. Two live rivals are **separated** when a non-retracted Result gives them different verdicts, and `hyp show Q` lists the pairs that are not; exhaustiveness is a property of the cases run on the candidates (see Limit), never of the set of rivals, which the owner may reserve. A live rival is live and not contradicted ([spec §7.1](replay-spec.md#71-hypothesis-status-first-matching-rule-wins)); the one-rival refusal and the one-rival and D1 signals read the live rivals of an Experiment's parent at its add ([spec §8](replay-spec.md#8-projection-what-replay-returns), Rivals at add).
96:A node, `R-`, under an Experiment, that records what a run observed: a verdict per target of its Experiment, an observation, evidence pointers and any limits ([spec §4](replay-spec.md#4-event-types-closed-set)). It is recorded or retracted, and a retracted Result no longer counts. In code: `replay.Res`, which holds its status, pins, questionable flag and uncontained reasons, in `Projection.Results`.
144:Retired by ADR 0019. It was the `confirm` event in which a role judged a select `sufficient` or `insufficient`; the last use was the owner's confirm of a scope-change select. `hyp confirm` exits 2. An old owner confirm replays only the limits it accepted ([spec §4](replay-spec.md#4-event-types-closed-set)), and an old verifier confirm applies nothing. The owner still "confirms" in plain speech when they choose or accept.
145:_Avoid_: approve, review; verdict (alone: a confirm's answer was a confirm verdict)
155:Retired by ADR 0015. It was the role that confirmed every select, independently of the actor who made it. Old verifier confirms replay as history and apply nothing, and `hyp confirm` is retired (ADR 0019). Any actor may still review: a defect is recorded as a Result, a retract or a limit. In code: `event.RoleVerifier`, read only from old logs.
156:_Avoid_: reviewer, checker (as a role)
159:The person hyp asks to act on real choices, and the role they act in. The owner adds the Goal with its lines, and then answers what the ledger lists under Awaiting owner: a reading or a referred limit with an Answer, and a choice between candidates (`choose:`). Whoever runs the tree records a choice as the select, with the owner's words in `--why`; the tree holds what was chosen, but not who chose it ([ADR 0015](adr/0015-the-select-is-the-gate.md)). hyp does not authenticate actors, so an owner act records that someone wrote an answer; that the owner stood behind it rests on the procedure. The owner's role and what they never do are stated in [principles.md](principles.md#7-who-does-what), and the moves in [spec §8.2](replay-spec.md#82-keyed-items-limits-lines-and-readings). In code: `event.Answer`; `event.RoleOwner` on old owner checkpoints.
163:The owner's act, its own event type (ADR 0020): `answers` for readings, `accepts` and `returns` for referred limits, each item a key with the owner's words for it, and at least one key. It has no node, no summary, no why and no role, and owner and runner fields never mix in one event. One answer may settle keys of several Goals. An item in `answers` is a first answer of an open reading or a revision of an answered one, derived from the reading's state. An accept means only that this Goal does not run the case. `hyp answer` writes it; an old owner checkpoint's `closes`, `revises`, `accepts` and `returns` are read-only history that replay still applies ([spec §4](replay-spec.md#4-event-types-closed-set)). In code: `event.Answer`.
167:The runner's report on one Goal: a `summary` of where the work stands, `refers` that hand limits to the owner with why, or both, and a required `why`; an empty one is refused. `hyp status` prints its Goal's last one, never an old owner checkpoint, and a run records one at each stop. It holds no owner act: an old owner checkpoint's `role`, `closes`, `revises`, `accepts`, `returns` and `lines` are read-only history that replay applies and no command writes (owner decision of 2026-11-11). In code: `event.Checkpoint`.
170:**Limit**:
171:A case the Goal covers that no check has yet run on a Hypothesis. It is a keyed item with two births and one life: a Result records a limit its run left uncovered, keyed `<result-id>#<n>` (ADR 0016), and the owner records a line of the Goal, keyed `G-<goal-id>#<n>` (see Line). Its one job is to name the next case to run: an Experiment aims at it (`--aims`), and a later Result that runs the case on the candidates closes it (`--closes`), so its verdicts separate the rivals. A runner refers a limit that no test within the Goal can close, or whose case is void for every candidate (`hyp checkpoint --refers K=WHY`), which moves it from the runner's Owed items to Awaiting owner. The owner answers the refer with an Answer: accepts it (`hyp answer --accept K=TEXT`), so this Goal does not run the case and a later Goal may carry it by citing the key, or returns it (`--returns K=TEXT`) when the Goal covers its case, which makes it the runner's again; a return also reopens an accepted limit, and an accept needs a refer first. One move table states each move, from which state and by whom ([spec §8.2](replay-spec.md#82-keyed-items-limits-lines-and-readings)). A close records that the case ran, whatever the verdicts, and a limit's category is never stored: it is what its closers' verdicts, an accept, and the latest refer or return say. A limit's hand (the latest refer, return or accept) and its closers are two facts, and an **open** limit is one neither closed nor accepted; open is said of a Result's limit only. An open limit is owed while its question has a candidate, whichever Hypotheses its Result judged, so the select waits on it ([spec §8](replay-spec.md#8-projection-what-replay-returns), Limits). Other notes a run makes have homes of their own: the scope of a run goes in the Experiment body, a procedure note or a commit goes in the observation with the commit in a cited file, and a premise is a `depends_on` edge. In code: `replay.Limit`.
175:A limit the owner records on the Goal: a case every candidate must meet, keyed `G-<goal-id>#<n>`. A Goal's lines come with its add (`hyp add goal --line TEXT`), and no later event adds one (ADR 0020); an old Goal's lines, written on its first owner checkpoint, keep their keys. A line may cite 0 to 10 keys settled when it is written (`--cite N=KEY`): a line, an accepted or closed limit, an answered reading, or a selected or contradicted Hypothesis. What a cite means (carried, forbidden, applied or realised) is derived from the key's state at the line's place in the log, and a later change is only a `hyp check` warning. A line is never edited: what it means is a reading and the owner's answer; a line the Goal no longer needs is referred by the runner and accepted by the owner; a case under a line is a limit, returned by the owner when the Goal covers it; a new line or a new purpose is a new Goal, which may sit in the same store. A line is neither open nor closed: `hyp status` prints its hand when it has one, `covered on Q-…` or `uncovered on Q-…: H-…` for each top-level question with a candidate (see Coverage), and the Results that ran it. A line is owed as a `limit` item on each live top-level question of its own Goal where it is uncovered, and holds that question's select. A verdict is per Hypothesis, never per line: a Result that closes several lines and contradicts a Hypothesis says the cases ran and the Hypothesis failed, not which line, and its observation says which check failed. `hyp status` prints the lines under LINES, and `hyp show G-…#n` prints one ([spec §8](replay-spec.md#8-projection-what-replay-returns), Lines). In code: a `replay.Limit` whose `Question` is empty, and its `Cites`.
179:A finding, often from a run's review, that is a case of none of the Goal's lines and asks no question about what a line means. It is not a limit, since a limit is a case the Goal covers, so it gets no tree event, no refer and no accept, and it never holds the select. The runner names it in its stop checkpoint's summary and its last message as a possible new Goal or issue, and the owner decides at global scope whether to add one. A defect in text the run changed and may edit is not one: the run fixes it with a commit.
180:_Avoid_: limit, refer (for a case no line covers), side note
183:An item created as one entry inside its parent's event and addressed as `<parent>#<n>` or `<parent>#r<n>`: a limit or a reading inside a Result, or a line of the Goal. Its text is fixed, it takes no edge, and it is gone when its Result is retracted. Only other events move its state, and one move table per kind says which move applies from which state and by whom ([spec §8.2](replay-spec.md#82-keyed-items-limits-lines-and-readings)). It is not a node: it has no add event, no title and no status of its own. In code: `internal/replay/keyed.go`.
191:The ledger `hyp status` prints under OWED: each item of open work on a question and who owes it, the runner; the owner's items print under Awaiting owner ([spec §8.1](replay-spec.md#81-ledger-what-the-tree-owes)). OWED is per Goal: `hyp status G-…` prints one Goal's, and in a store with many Goals `hyp status` prints a GOALS table with what each Goal's runner owes. A line of the Goal is owed on each live top-level question that has a candidate no closer covers, as a `limit` item keyed `G-…#n`. A move never crosses Goals: only an item's own Goal refers, aims at, closes or applies it. An answered question owes only its limit, reading, referred and premise items. It is derived, never stored, and owing an item changes no status; `hyp select` reads it to admit a select. When the runner owes nothing, OWED ends with `runner owes nothing: stop and report to the owner`, the stop a run reads. In code: `replay.Projection.Owed`.
195:Where a question's decision stands, derived by one rule, first match wins, and never stored ([spec §8.1](replay-spec.md#81-ledger-what-the-tree-owes)): **closed** (answered, deferred or withdrawn; a select that stands is an answered question), **waits** (on runner work, an open reading with a reach, a referred limit, a premise, or a sub-question, in that order), **no candidate**, or **owed** (the runner's select of a lone candidate, or the owner's choice). The ledger owes a select or a choice only on an owed turn; `hyp select` refuses with the first thing the turn waits on; `hyp status` prints a `waits on …` line for each thing other than runner work. In code: `replay.Turn`, from `Projection.Turn`.
211:A limit or answered reading an Experiment is planned to settle, named with `hyp add exp --aims`. An aim is intent: it moves the item to `in_progress`, and to `aimed_not_settled` when every aiming Experiment has a Result and none closed or applied it. Only a Result's `--closes` or `--applies` settles the item, and settling it never answers a question.
438:Every concept hyp has, and everything a user who installs hyp into another repository runs, loads or reads there. A concept stays core when self-review is what tests it.
441:**Self-review**:
442:The recipes this repository keeps to test hyp, whatever repository the runner works on, with the inputs only they use. Investigating hyp is an activity, not a scope: a tree about hyp takes the scope of its question, and a tree about another project is a self-review input.

content.content:
---
name: hyp-goal-run
description: "Run a hyp tree under an owner's Goal and met rule as an unattended /goal, for a discovery Goal or a build Goal: act only on what OWED says the runner owes, test before asking, write readings the owner can answer, reassess the targets under the owner's answers, and stop with a report the owner can read from hyp status. Use when a /goal prompt names this skill, such as the one hyp prompt prints."
---

The `/goal` prompt names the tree, your actor, the Goal, the stop and the Goal body's constraints; `hyp prompt <goal-id> --actor <actor>` prints it from the log. This skill says how to work until that stop. Use it with the hyp-prototype skill, which says how to add Questions, Hypotheses, Experiments and Results, and the hyp-verification skill, which says how to run an Experiment.

## Start

- Read the Goal first with `hyp show <goal-id>`, including its checkpoints, because `hyp status` does not print its met rule.
- Everything you need is in the tree. Do not read session logs, reports or memory about earlier runs.
- The Goal's body states the run's constraints under three headings: `May change:` (what you may write, and how), `Read only:` (what you may read but never change) and `Never:` (acts you never take). Obey them. A `/goal` prompt may narrow them, never widen them. If a step needs something they forbid, refer it with a reason or record a reading, and stop.
- A store may hold many Goals. Then `hyp status` prints only a GOALS table and one Awaiting owner list, so run `hyp status <goal-id>` wherever this skill says `hyp status`: OWED, LINES, the stop line and the last checkpoint are per Goal. Name the Goal with `--goal <goal-id>` on `hyp checkpoint`.
- Print `hyp status` at the end of every turn.

## Work

Act on what OWED in `hyp status` says the runner owes, and on nothing else. Plan only the next Experiment.

- Use the Goal's must-fail cases as known-answer flaw cases, in the owner's terms.
- The recipe's checks may exist before the verdict rule, because `hyp add exp` pins them. Write and run no candidate until the rule is recorded on the Experiment.
- Try a new or changed check only on its cases' stand-ins, never on a candidate, until the rule is recorded. If a candidate shows a check is wrong anyway, do not just fix the check: write the case that shows it, in the Goal's terms with the outcome it must give, in a new version, and name that case in the Experiment body. A sentence that discloses a trial run pins nothing.
- `hyp record` and `hyp check` warn when a Result's text disagrees with its cited files: a verdict that a cited `verdict:` line contradicts, or a commit or hash in the observation or a limit that no cited file holds. Fix each one with a new Result that cites the file; a Result cannot change after it is recorded.

## Build Goals

A build Goal's candidate is a commit. Its practice:

- Each commit you test is one Hypothesis under the Goal's question, with the branch and the commit in its title. Tie its subject before the run with `hyp subject <H> --base <commit>`. A fix is a new commit and a new Hypothesis that supersedes the old one (`hyp supersede <new> --old <old>`).
- Write the tree with the installed hyp. Compile the candidate to a separate path, and never replace an installed binary.
- Pin the gate as a recipe when the repository keeps one, so a script decides the verdict. When none does, the Experiment on a commit uses `--recipe none --rubric reading`: its body states the gate as the rule, and the Result cites the gate's logs.
- Before you run anything, write each Experiment's verdict rule in its body: the Goal's lines it aims at, red on the base and green on the candidate for each new test, a removal check for each refusal (remove the refusal and show which test fails), and `go vet ./...` and `go test ./... -count=1`, or the repository's own gate. For skill text, run the original and the candidate skills on the same eval cases.
- Keep the logs under `.tree/evidence/<E-id>/` and cite them in the Result.
- Before the stop, ask a fresh subagent for one review of each candidate commit's diff against the design and the Goal's lines. Give it the code, the lines and the keys already settled, with the owner's words; do not give it your conclusion. Ask it to label each finding with the line it is a case of, or none.
- Sort each finding: a case of a line is a `--limit` you close or, only if void, refer; a question about a line's meaning is a reading; a defect in text you may edit is a fix commit; anything else is an out-of-Goal finding, named in the stop checkpoint, and it never holds the select.
- The run may push its branch and open or update one PR. It never merges.

## Before a trade-off

Before a Question goes to the owner as a trade-off, add one structure that is not among the candidates, and the cheapest variant of each contradicted rival that would hold. Run them through a new version of the pinned recipe and record the Result. If a new structure holds every check, say in a checkpoint that the rule does not decide this Question.

## Readings

- When a verdict rests on your reading of a Goal line, write the other reading as a strict check: a separate named command in the recipe, with its own known answers, that sets no verdict. Say so in the Experiment's verdict rule, and run it on the same candidates. Record the reading with `hyp record --reading`, naming the check and which candidates fail it. If the recipe cannot test the other reading, say that in the reading.
- When a verdict rests on the word of a reading that is still open under AWAITING OWNER, or on an owner answer another Result already reads, record the same reading on that Result too, word for word, with the same `--reading-of` key if it has one: a reading holds only its own Result's Question, and hyp prints identical readings as one question and warns when the owner answers only one. Record a copy only on a Result that judged a Hypothesis whose verdict differs from the strict check's outcome for it: a `supports` the check fails, or a `contradicts` the check passes. A Result whose judged Hypotheses the check gives the same outcome as the verdict gets no copy. The owner answers every copy in one answer, because `--answer` is repeatable.
- Before you record a reading, look for a test that can decide it. If a test fits the Goal's lines, write it, run it under the verdict rule, and record no reading. If a test needs a new Goal line, name the test, the fact it measures and the line in the reading, and ask the owner whether to run it. Ask the owner to choose a meaning only when no test can decide, and say why none can.
- Write each reading in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English: short sentences, active verbs, one meaning for each word, and the Goal's words for things. Use this form:

  ```text
  <Goal line>: "<the words>" has two meanings. Meaning 1: <...>. Meaning 2: <...>. This run used meaning <n>. <Check> tests meaning <n>; <candidates> fail it. Question: <one question the owner can answer in their own words>?
  ```

  Give one small example of each meaning, in the Goal's terms. If the line does not have two meanings, state the case it does not clearly cover, then the question. A reading holds at most 600 characters.

## Owner answers

- When the owner answers a reading, record it with their exact words, `hyp answer --answer "<R-id>#r<n>=<their words>" --actor <owner-actor>`, and treat their answer as the meaning of that line. If the owner's words answer a reading but do not name it, ask which reading before you write; an answer must name its key. Do not leave a question only in chat.
- If the owner's answer itself has two meanings, record a reading of that answer with `hyp record --reading-of <R-id>#r<n>="<the form above>"`. It narrows the answer and never reopens it; the answer stays in force.
- Only the owner changes an answer. When they give new words for a reading they already answered, record them with the same `hyp answer --answer "<R-id>#r<n>=<their new words>"`; hyp derives that it is a revision. The earlier answer and the Results that applied it stay. Apply the new answer with a Result that `--applies` it, and test a successor (`hyp supersede`) of any Hypothesis the old answer contradicted.
- A limit the owner accepts is recorded with `hyp answer --accept "<key>=<their words>" --actor <owner-actor>`, and a return with `--returns`. hyp admits an accept only of a limit you referred, and never under your actor.

## Reassess

Apply each answered reading that `hyp status` lists under OWED as `apply answer`, and act on each limit it lists.

1. For each answer, write one line: the owner's words, the check, and the candidates that fail it. If the owner is in this session, show the lines and wait for their yes. If not, write the lines in the Experiment's body.
2. For each Question, add one Experiment that names each answer it applies with `--aims`, and fix how its verdicts are decided before you run it: a rubric from `rubrics/` (`--rubric <name>@<version>`, a new rubric version when the answer changes the rule) or `--rubric reading` with the rule in its body. A recipe measures and never prints a verdict. To reassess records an earlier run kept, pin them with `--records .tree/evidence/<E-id>` and `--recipe none`. If an outcome is already known, say so in the rule. Give a verdict on every target, `inconclusive` when the run could not decide. Record its Result with `--applies` for each answer it applied. Old Results stay as they are.
3. If applying an answer raises a new question about what a Goal line or the owner's answer means, record it with `hyp record --reading` on that Result. A Result cannot change after it is recorded, so if it is already recorded, record a new Result under the same Experiment.
4. Act on each `limit` line under OWED, whichever Hypothesis its Result gave a verdict on: a limit is a case the Goal covers that no check ran. If a test within the Goal's lines can run the case on every candidate, add an Experiment with `--aims` at it, run it, and record `--closes` on the Result that ran the case. A close records that the case ran, whatever the verdicts: a candidate that fails the case is contradicted and the limit is still closed, so never write a rule that closes it only on a pass. A close covers every case the limit's text names; `hyp record` prints that text when it closes. Record each case you did not run as a new `--limit` on the closing Result, and refer that new key when its case is void or outside the Goal's lines. A claim that a case is void, out of scope or covered elsewhere is a limit and a refer, never a sentence in a body or an observation. When that claim rests on your reading of a Goal line, put the reading in the refer's text. Write one case per `--limit`. If no such test can, or the case is void for every candidate, refer it with your reason: `hyp checkpoint --refers "<key>=<why no test within the Goal can close it, or why the case is void>" --why "..."`; hyp refuses a refer with no reason. When the owner returns a referred limit, it is an ordinary `limit` line again.
5. End with the candidates left under each Question: none, one, or several, by alias.
6. Select only when OWED lists `select` for that Question: `hyp select <Q-id> <H-id> --why "..."`. Never confirm a select. Do not change the Goal or add new structures unless the owner asks.

## Goal lines

- The Goal's lines are limits keyed on the Goal, `G-<id>#<n>`; `hyp status` prints them under LINES. A Goal's lines come with its add and no later event adds one. If the Goal's body states lines and none is typed, they cannot be added to this Goal: tell the owner, who may add a new Goal with them (`hyp add goal … --line "<line>"`). Do not write them for the owner.
- A line is owed as a `limit` on each top-level Question with a candidate no closer covers. Run its case like any limit: aim at it with `--aims G-<id>#<n>`, and record `--closes G-<id>#<n>` on each Result that ran the case. A Result covers a candidate it gave a verdict on, or one whose whole subject (base, patch and files) one of the Result's cited runs holds, so tie each candidate before the run: `hyp subject <H> [PATH…] --base <commit> [--patch FILE]`.
- A line is never edited. What a line means is a reading. A line no test within the Goal can run is a refer, and the owner accepts or returns it. A new line or a new purpose is a new Goal, so a new tree: tell the owner, and do not write it.

## Stop

Stop on the clauses the `/goal` prompt names. Stopping is not success.

1. Before your last message, record a runner checkpoint, so the fork does not live only in chat; the owner reads `hyp status`, which prints the last checkpoint, each reading in full and what each copy's answer can touch. Do not restate a reading's meanings in the checkpoint:

   ```text
   hyp checkpoint --goal <goal-id> --summary "Stopped: <stop clause>. Waiting for the owner: <the keys under AWAITING OWNER>. Out-of-Goal findings: <one short phrase each, or none>" --why "<why>"
   ```

   An out-of-Goal finding is a case of none of the Goal's lines: it gets no limit, no refer and no reading, and it never holds the select. Name each one in the checkpoint so it lives in the log, not only in chat. A defect in text you changed and may edit is not one: fix it with a commit before the stop.

2. Your last message repeats the checkpoint, and lists each line under LINES by its key, with the Results that ran it, and names each question where OWED still owes a line. A run that ends with lines owed is a normal result.

3. Then list every owner item with the exact command the owner runs: each item under AWAITING OWNER, each out-of-Goal finding (a new Goal or an issue), merging the PR, reinstalling hyp, and each personal skill that names a command the change altered.

## Never

- Never change the Goal or its met rule.
- Never record a choice the owner reserved, and never record an owner answer unless the owner gave those words in this session.

Every write command needs --why and an actor (--actor or $HYP_ACTOR).
Statuses are derived from events; no command can set one.

setup:
  init                                   create .tree in the current directory
  version                                print the hyp version

write:
  add goal --title T [--body B] [--alias A] [--line L]... [--cite N=KEY]...
  add dq   --parent REF --title T [--body B] [--alias A]
  add hyp  --parent REF --title T [--body B] [--alias A] [--subject PATH]...
  add exp  --parent REF --title T --recipe NAME@V|none [--rubric NAME@V|reading] [--records PATH]... [--target REF|none]... [--alias A]
  record   --exp REF [--verdict REF=supports|contradicts|inconclusive]... --observation O [--evidence P]... [--limit L]... [--closes R#N]...
  retract REF | abandon REF | reaffirm REF
  supersede NEW --old OLD
  amend HYP --body B                     revise a Hypothesis body
  subject HYP [PATH...] [--base C]       tie a Hypothesis to the base and files that embody its claim
  link FROM depends_on|external_ref TO   unlink FROM TYPE TO
  select DQ [HYP]                        admitted only when hyp status owes it (no HYP: print the suggestion only)
  unselect DQ | defer DQ | withdraw DQ|EXP | resume DQ
  checkpoint [--summary S] [--goal G] [--refers K[=TEXT]]...   the runner's report: a summary, refers, or both
  answer [--answer R#rN=TEXT]... [--accept K=TEXT]... [--returns K=TEXT]...   the owner's act; no --why

read (REF/TIME: an event id, a node ref, or an RFC3339 time):
  status [--as-of REF|TIME] [--max-lines N] [--live]   orientation screen, 60 lines by default; --live hides contradicted rivals
  show REF|R-id#n|G-id#n [--as-of REF|TIME]  one node, or one limit or line, in full, with its history
  diff --since REF|TIME                       status changes and events since a point
  render --markdown [--as-of REF|TIME]        the whole tree as Markdown, untruncated
  check                                       rejected events, bad lines, warnings
  signals [--json]                            design marks for the whole tree: one-rival, D1

bundle (a recipe in recipes/ or a rubric in rubrics/; a name lives in one library):

3:The words hyp uses for its tree, its recipes and its sandboxes. The specs ([replay-spec.md](replay-spec.md), [sandbox-spec.md](sandbox-spec.md)) and the recipe format define the rules; this file only fixes which word means what, links the rule's section instead of restating it, and names the Go type that owns each concept where one exists. It also names the two scopes of this repository, core and self-review, and the test that puts an item in one; [core-and-self-review.md](core-and-self-review.md) maps the repository onto them.
30:Everything replay derives from a store's events: each node, a derived record per node kind (Hypothesis, Question, Experiment and Result) with its own status word, the Goal's state, rejections, limits and selections ([spec §8](replay-spec.md#8-projection-what-replay-returns)). Nothing stores it; every read replays (ADR 0006). In code: `replay.Projection`.
34:The root node of a tree, `G-`: what the investigation is for. A store holds many Goals, and a tree is the view of one Goal and every node whose parents lead to it (ADR 0020); each Goal has its own lines, OWED and coverage. A Goal is complete when every live DesignQuestion under it is answered ([spec §7.5](replay-spec.md#75-goal)). Its lines are the limits the owner records on it (see Line); the owner's "met" is a complete Goal with no line under OWED, read from `hyp status`, and hyp stores no word for it. No one changes a Goal once it is written: its lines come with its add, and a new purpose is a new Goal, which may sit in the same store and cite the keys it carries over (see Line). By what its candidate is, a Goal is a discovery Goal or a build Goal; hyp stores no kind, and the same events, rules and ledger serve both (ADR 0020).
46:A Goal whose candidate is a commit: building is a Goal like any other. A line asserts one property of the candidate, decided by its own tests or one pinned instrument: `[P]` pins what a valid input produces, and `[N]` pins that a forbidden state is refused. Each commit is a Hypothesis whose subject is the base plus that commit's change, and a fix is a new Hypothesis that supersedes it. Each Experiment's verdict rule asks for red on base and green on the candidate; the base of the red run's subject is where the build starts, and the Goal records no start commit. A finding of a run's review that is a case of a line is a limit; one that is not is an out-of-Goal finding. A change to a skill is a build Goal too (ADR 0021).
65:The section of `hyp status` that names the one step due from the owner on each question the Frontier prints: `choose: H…, H…` when they should choose between the candidates and the runner owes nothing on the question. A question the Frontier does not print asks nothing, and the choice is owed again once it prints. It also lists every open reading, which blocks nothing, and every referred limit on a candidate. `hyp status G-…` lists one Goal's items; in a store with many Goals, `hyp status` prints one Awaiting owner list, grouped by Goal.
76:**Open limits**:
77:The section of `hyp status` that lists every open limit, whatever the state of its question and whether the Frontier prints it. It is a list, not open work: the open work in it is what Owed and Awaiting owner name.
80:Another Hypothesis under the same DesignQuestion. Two live rivals are **separated** when a non-retracted Result gives them different verdicts, and `hyp show Q` lists the pairs that are not; exhaustiveness is a property of the cases run on the candidates (see Limit), never of the set of rivals, which the owner may reserve. A live rival is live and not contradicted ([spec §7.1](replay-spec.md#71-hypothesis-status-first-matching-rule-wins)); the one-rival refusal and the one-rival and D1 signals read the live rivals of an Experiment's parent at its add ([spec §8](replay-spec.md#8-projection-what-replay-returns), Rivals at add).
96:A node, `R-`, under an Experiment, that records what a run observed: a verdict per target of its Experiment, an observation, evidence pointers and any limits ([spec §4](replay-spec.md#4-event-types-closed-set)). It is recorded or retracted, and a retracted Result no longer counts. In code: `replay.Res`, which holds its status, pins, questionable flag and uncontained reasons, in `Projection.Results`.
144:Retired by ADR 0019. It was the `confirm` event in which a role judged a select `sufficient` or `insufficient`; the last use was the owner's confirm of a scope-change select. `hyp confirm` exits 2. An old owner confirm replays only the limits it accepted ([spec §4](replay-spec.md#4-event-types-closed-set)), and an old verifier confirm applies nothing. The owner still "confirms" in plain speech when they choose or accept.
145:_Avoid_: approve, review; verdict (alone: a confirm's answer was a confirm verdict)
155:Retired by ADR 0015. It was the role that confirmed every select, independently of the actor who made it. Old verifier confirms replay as history and apply nothing, and `hyp confirm` is retired (ADR 0019). Any actor may still review: a defect is recorded as a Result, a retract or a limit. In code: `event.RoleVerifier`, read only from old logs.
156:_Avoid_: reviewer, checker (as a role)
159:The person hyp asks to act on real choices, and the role they act in. The owner adds the Goal with its lines, and then answers what the ledger lists under Awaiting owner: a reading or a referred limit with an Answer, and a choice between candidates (`choose:`). Whoever runs the tree records a choice as the select, with the owner's words in `--why`; the tree holds what was chosen, but not who chose it ([ADR 0015](adr/0015-the-select-is-the-gate.md)). hyp does not authenticate actors, so an owner act records that someone wrote an answer; that the owner stood behind it rests on the procedure. The owner's role and what they never do are stated in [principles.md](principles.md#7-who-does-what), and the moves in [spec §8.2](replay-spec.md#82-keyed-items-limits-lines-and-readings). In code: `event.Answer`; `event.RoleOwner` on old owner checkpoints.
163:The owner's act, its own event type (ADR 0020): `answers` for readings, `accepts` and `returns` for referred limits, each item a key with the owner's words for it, and at least one key. It has no node, no summary, no why and no role, and owner and runner fields never mix in one event. One answer may settle keys of several Goals. An item in `answers` is a first answer of an open reading or a revision of an answered one, derived from the reading's state. An accept means only that this Goal does not run the case. `hyp answer` writes it; an old owner checkpoint's `closes`, `revises`, `accepts` and `returns` are read-only history that replay still applies ([spec §4](replay-spec.md#4-event-types-closed-set)). In code: `event.Answer`.
167:The runner's report on one Goal: a `summary` of where the work stands, `refers` that hand limits to the owner with why, or both, and a required `why`; an empty one is refused. `hyp status` prints its Goal's last one, never an old owner checkpoint, and a run records one at each stop. It holds no owner act: an old owner checkpoint's `role`, `closes`, `revises`, `accepts`, `returns` and `lines` are read-only history that replay applies and no command writes (owner decision of 2026-11-11). In code: `event.Checkpoint`.
170:**Limit**:
171:A case the Goal covers that no check has yet run on a Hypothesis. It is a keyed item with two births and one life: a Result records a limit its run left uncovered, keyed `<result-id>#<n>` (ADR 0016), and the owner records a line of the Goal, keyed `G-<goal-id>#<n>` (see Line). Its one job is to name the next case to run: an Experiment aims at it (`--aims`), and a later Result that runs the case on the candidates closes it (`--closes`), so its verdicts separate the rivals. A runner refers a limit that no test within the Goal can close, or whose case is void for every candidate (`hyp checkpoint --refers K=WHY`), which moves it from the runner's Owed items to Awaiting owner. The owner answers the refer with an Answer: accepts it (`hyp answer --accept K=TEXT`), so this Goal does not run the case and a later Goal may carry it by citing the key, or returns it (`--returns K=TEXT`) when the Goal covers its case, which makes it the runner's again; a return also reopens an accepted limit, and an accept needs a refer first. One move table states each move, from which state and by whom ([spec §8.2](replay-spec.md#82-keyed-items-limits-lines-and-readings)). A close records that the case ran, whatever the verdicts, and a limit's category is never stored: it is what its closers' verdicts, an accept, and the latest refer or return say. A limit's hand (the latest refer, return or accept) and its closers are two facts, and an **open** limit is one neither closed nor accepted; open is said of a Result's limit only. An open limit is owed while its question has a candidate, whichever Hypotheses its Result judged, so the select waits on it ([spec §8](replay-spec.md#8-projection-what-replay-returns), Limits). Other notes a run makes have homes of their own: the scope of a run goes in the Experiment body, a procedure note or a commit goes in the observation with the commit in a cited file, and a premise is a `depends_on` edge. In code: `replay.Limit`.
175:A limit the owner records on the Goal: a case every candidate must meet, keyed `G-<goal-id>#<n>`. A Goal's lines come with its add (`hyp add goal --line TEXT`), and no later event adds one (ADR 0020); an old Goal's lines, written on its first owner checkpoint, keep their keys. A line may cite 0 to 10 keys settled when it is written (`--cite N=KEY`): a line, an accepted or closed limit, an answered reading, or a selected or contradicted Hypothesis. What a cite means (carried, forbidden, applied or realised) is derived from the key's state at the line's place in the log, and a later change is only a `hyp check` warning. A line is never edited: what it means is a reading and the owner's answer; a line the Goal no longer needs is referred by the runner and accepted by the owner; a case under a line is a limit, returned by the owner when the Goal covers it; a new line or a new purpose is a new Goal, which may sit in the same store. A line is neither open nor closed: `hyp status` prints its hand when it has one, `covered on Q-…` or `uncovered on Q-…: H-…` for each top-level question with a candidate (see Coverage), and the Results that ran it. A line is owed as a `limit` item on each live top-level question of its own Goal where it is uncovered, and holds that question's select. A verdict is per Hypothesis, never per line: a Result that closes several lines and contradicts a Hypothesis says the cases ran and the Hypothesis failed, not which line, and its observation says which check failed. `hyp status` prints the lines under LINES, and `hyp show G-…#n` prints one ([spec §8](replay-spec.md#8-projection-what-replay-returns), Lines). In code: a `replay.Limit` whose `Question` is empty, and its `Cites`.
179:A finding, often from a run's review, that is a case of none of the Goal's lines and asks no question about what a line means. It is not a limit, since a limit is a case the Goal covers, so it gets no tree event, no refer and no accept, and it never holds the select. The runner names it in its stop checkpoint's summary and its last message as a possible new Goal or issue, and the owner decides at global scope whether to add one. A defect in text the run changed and may edit is not one: the run fixes it with a commit.
180:_Avoid_: limit, refer (for a case no line covers), side note
183:An item created as one entry inside its parent's event and addressed as `<parent>#<n>` or `<parent>#r<n>`: a limit or a reading inside a Result, or a line of the Goal. Its text is fixed, it takes no edge, and it is gone when its Result is retracted. Only other events move its state, and one move table per kind says which move applies from which state and by whom ([spec §8.2](replay-spec.md#82-keyed-items-limits-lines-and-readings)). It is not a node: it has no add event, no title and no status of its own. In code: `internal/replay/keyed.go`.
191:The ledger `hyp status` prints under OWED: each item of open work on a question and who owes it, the runner; the owner's items print under Awaiting owner ([spec §8.1](replay-spec.md#81-ledger-what-the-tree-owes)). OWED is per Goal: `hyp status G-…` prints one Goal's, and in a store with many Goals `hyp status` prints a GOALS table with what each Goal's runner owes. A line of the Goal is owed on each live top-level question that has a candidate no closer covers, as a `limit` item keyed `G-…#n`. A move never crosses Goals: only an item's own Goal refers, aims at, closes or applies it. An answered question owes only its limit, reading, referred and premise items. It is derived, never stored, and owing an item changes no status; `hyp select` reads it to admit a select. When the runner owes nothing, OWED ends with `runner owes nothing: stop and report to the owner`, the stop a run reads. In code: `replay.Projection.Owed`.
195:Where a question's decision stands, derived by one rule, first match wins, and never stored ([spec §8.1](replay-spec.md#81-ledger-what-the-tree-owes)): **closed** (answered, deferred or withdrawn; a select that stands is an answered question), **waits** (on runner work, an open reading with a reach, a referred limit, a premise, or a sub-question, in that order), **no candidate**, or **owed** (the runner's select of a lone candidate, or the owner's choice). The ledger owes a select or a choice only on an owed turn; `hyp select` refuses with the first thing the turn waits on; `hyp status` prints a `waits on …` line for each thing other than runner work. In code: `replay.Turn`, from `Projection.Turn`.
211:A limit or answered reading an Experiment is planned to settle, named with `hyp add exp --aims`. An aim is intent: it moves the item to `in_progress`, and to `aimed_not_settled` when every aiming Experiment has a Result and none closed or applied it. Only a Result's `--closes` or `--applies` settles the item, and settling it never answers a question.
438:Every concept hyp has, and everything a user who installs hyp into another repository runs, loads or reads there. A concept stays core when self-review is what tests it.
441:**Self-review**:
442:The recipes this repository keeps to test hyp, whatever repository the runner works on, with the inputs only they use. Investigating hyp is an activity, not a scope: a tree about hyp takes the scope of its question, and a tree about another project is a self-review input.

Supersedes in part [ADR 0007](0007-records-start-at-230.md) (the skill-text gate's replay instrument), [ADR 0010](0010-a-record-keeps-or-identifies-what-a-replay-needs.md) (the follow-up that rebuilds `skill-text-arms` Arms from patches) and [ADR 0015](0015-the-select-is-the-gate.md) (the frozen verifier recipes).

# A skill change is a build Goal

AGENTS.md gated skill text apart from code. A skill-text change shipped only when a session replay from the event's store cut showed the failure in 3 or more of 5 trials without the change and in 1 or fewer of 5 with it, and nothing shipped when no cut reproduced the failure. Its one instrument, `recipes/skill-text-arms@5` with the rubric `rubrics/skill-text-gate@1`, replays the id-citation tree's e-arms with `hyp-prototype` and `hyp-verification` loaded. It cannot reach a skill that runs before any tree exists, such as `hyp-owner-grill`, or one that spans a whole `/goal` run, such as `hyp-goal-run` and `hyp-owner-answer`. For those skills the rule was a permanent freeze, and a new skill needed its own exception. [how-hyp-improves-itself.md](../how-hyp-improves-itself.md) had already found that replay studies of skill text decided nothing, because agents with the skill loaded rarely made the mistakes they counted.

Owner decision on 2026-11-11 (#134): building is a Goal like any other (ADR 0020), and a change to `skills/` is building. The special gate was context that led agents to design gate policy instead of applying that model.

## Decision

- **A change to `skills/`, a new skill included, is a build Goal like any code change.** Its candidate is the commit; its lines state the skill's behaviour; each line is checked by its own test or by an instrument the Goal builds, red on base, and the select ends it. For a new skill, base is no skill.
- **How a skill is tested is that Goal's choice**, settled in its grill. One choice is ak-skill-creator's eval: cases in its `evals.json` format kept as a file of a `recipes/<skill>-eval@N` bundle, graded by `eval_skill.py`, which is named on the command's `External:` line and never copied. hyp keeps no instrument and no threshold for skill text as such.
- **A skill error seen during another run** is an out-of-Goal finding, or a new Goal by promotion. No audit cadence is kept.
- **Unchanged:** a change still needs a real event, and a failure detectable from the tree goes into the binary as a refusal or a warning, gated by `go test`.
- **Removed:** `recipes/skill-text-arms@3`, `@4` and `@5`, `rubrics/skill-text-gate@1`, and the retired `recipes/verifier-brief-arms@1` and `recipes/verifier-audit-arms@1`.

## Alternatives

- **Replay from eval cases instead of a store cut, keeping 3 of 5 against 1 of 5.** Rejected: it keeps skill text apart from code, and the count is a test design that belongs to the Goal.
- **A standing audit after each real use of a skill.** Rejected: an error seen in a run already has a home, as an out-of-Goal finding or a new Goal.

## Consequences

- No published tree pins a removed recipe. `investigations/recipe-base` names `skill-text-arms` only as the held-out subject its runners authored, and `recipes/recipe-base-arms@1` carries its own copy of that method.
- The removed bundles stay in git history; an old Result that names one can still be read from there.
- `id-citation-arms`, `recipe-base-arms`, `recipe-authoring-arms` and `authoring-stops` are kept.

Supersedes in part [ADR 0007](0007-records-start-at-230.md) (the skill-text gate's replay instrument), [ADR 0010](0010-a-record-keeps-or-identifies-what-a-replay-needs.md) (the follow-up that rebuilds `skill-text-arms` Arms from patches) and [ADR 0015](0015-the-select-is-the-gate.md) (the frozen verifier recipes).

# A skill change is a build Goal

AGENTS.md gated skill text apart from code. A skill-text change shipped only when a session replay from the event's store cut showed the failure in 3 or more of 5 trials without the change and in 1 or fewer of 5 with it, and nothing shipped when no cut reproduced the failure. Its one instrument, `recipes/skill-text-arms@5` with the rubric `rubrics/skill-text-gate@1`, replays the id-citation tree's e-arms with `hyp-prototype` and `hyp-verification` loaded. It cannot reach a skill that runs before any tree exists, such as `hyp-owner-grill`, or one that spans a whole `/goal` run, such as `hyp-goal-run` and `hyp-owner-answer`. For those skills the rule was a permanent freeze, and a new skill needed its own exception. [how-hyp-improves-itself.md](../how-hyp-improves-itself.md) had already found that replay studies of skill text decided nothing, because agents with the skill loaded rarely made the mistakes they counted.

Owner decision on 2026-11-11 (#134): building is a Goal like any other (ADR 0020), and a change to `skills/` is building. The special gate was context that led agents to design gate policy instead of applying that model.

## Decision

- **A change to `skills/`, a new skill included, is a build Goal like any code change.** Its candidate is the commit; its lines state the skill's behaviour; each line is checked by its own test or by an instrument the Goal builds, red on base, and the select ends it. For a new skill, base is no skill.
- **How a skill is tested is that Goal's choice**, settled in its grill. One choice is ak-skill-creator's eval: cases in its `evals.json` format kept as a file of a `recipes/<skill>-eval@N` bundle, graded by `eval_skill.py`, which is named on the command's `External:` line and never copied. hyp keeps no instrument and no threshold for skill text as such.
- **A skill error seen during another run** is an out-of-Goal finding, or a new Goal by promotion. No audit cadence is kept.
- **Unchanged:** a change still needs a real event, and a failure detectable from the tree goes into the binary as a refusal or a warning, gated by `go test`.
- **Removed:** `recipes/skill-text-arms@3`, `@4` and `@5`, `rubrics/skill-text-gate@1`, and the retired `recipes/verifier-brief-arms@1` and `recipes/verifier-audit-arms@1`.

## Alternatives

- **Replay from eval cases instead of a store cut, keeping 3 of 5 against 1 of 5.** Rejected: it keeps skill text apart from code, and the count is a test design that belongs to the Goal.
- **A standing audit after each real use of a skill.** Rejected: an error seen in a run already has a home, as an out-of-Goal finding or a new Goal.

## Consequences

- No published tree pins a removed recipe. `investigations/recipe-base` names `skill-text-arms` only as the held-out subject its runners authored, and `recipes/recipe-base-arms@1` carries its own copy of that method.
- The removed bundles stay in git history; an old Result that names one can still be read from there.
- `id-citation-arms`, `recipe-base-arms`, `recipe-authoring-arms` and `authoring-stops` are kept.

content.text:
I did not use ak-context-engineering. It isn't installed here: `.claude/skills` and `~/.claude/skills` don't list it. The only match on this machine is a directory at `~/codingProjects/context-engineering`, which is outside this task, so I haven't read it. If you want it used, install it or tell me to read that directory. Then I'll name it in the Goal body as an optional method, and the run would apply it.

## One question (item 4)

Agreed. There is one DesignQuestion, with all six rivals under it: "Which change to the run practice keeps a review from being cut off by the budget or dragged out by small fixes?" Each rival body names its own starting point:

- **Run-1 and run-2 cuts:** H-name-at-stop, H-reserve-last, H-one-experiment and H-raise-budget.
- **Run-3 cut after R-JHBCWS:** H-probe-closes.
- **Final candidate `04142f3`:** H-whole-candidate. The body records your expectation that it loses on cost. It is still run, and it carries no preset verdict.
- **Control arm:** the unchanged skill at the same cut. It is not a Hypothesis. It gives each cost line its comparison.

## Your two aims (item 5)

You're right that the second aim had no line, and the first was only half covered. My "reviewed or named" line lets a rule pass by naming the gap, which doesn't keep the review inside the budget. I propose three lines:

1. **[P], aim 1.** At the first stop clause of a replayed run from the Hypothesis's cut, its last candidate commit has a review Result. Naming the gap does not satisfy this line. So H-name-at-stop alone is contradicted, which is honest, because naming doesn't make a review happen. It stays a part of combinations and becomes a line of the build Goal.
2. **[N], known answers.** A rule under which a finding that the real review reported as a case of a line (run 1's G1, G2 or K1) ends with no limit, no close, no fix commit and no name. Without it, "no review" would be the cheapest way to pass the cost line.
3. **[N], aim 2, the cost line.** The candidate's cost at its cut is at most 1.5 times the control's cost at that cut.

## How the cost is computed (item 5)

Here is my proposal for each part. The units are mine, so please check them.

- **Unit.** Results recorded from the cut until `hyp status` shows the select or "runner owes nothing". This is the budget's own unit, and the log gives the count without anyone judging it. The eval record's `tokens` field was `null` in E-NZR3GV, so a token count isn't available from that flow. Tokens are what would make H-whole-candidate expensive, so I'd note its token use as an observation but not use it in the line.
- **Restarts.** If a run hits its budget before the select, a new run starts with a fresh budget of the same size, as your run 2 did. The cost is the total across runs, so an arm that ends reviewed at its first stop but then loops on fixes still pays for the loop.
- **Trial cost.** One number per trial. A trial counts as hung and costs ∞ if it records 15 Results without reaching the select, runs past 45 minutes of wall clock, or is killed.
- **Median.** Sort the 3 trials' costs from lowest to highest, with ∞ last, and take the middle one. Two hangs out of three gives ∞.
- **The line.** A candidate fails if its median is ∞, or if 2 × candidate median is greater than 3 × control median. If the control median is ∞, any finite candidate passes. I use integer arithmetic so there is no rounding; control 2 allows up to 3.
- **Runs.** 3 trials per arm per start, on Sonnet, replayed from the cut, with an independent grader.

## Questions for you

- **A.** Do you accept line 1 without the naming escape?
- **B.** Is "Results until the select, across restarts" what you mean by "goes on and on", or do you want tokens or wall clock instead?
- **C.** Are 15 Results and 45 minutes the right ceiling for a hang?
- **D.** The count is about 42 trials, and each is a chain of runs: 5 arms × 3 trials at each of the run-1 and run-2 cuts, plus 2 × 3 at each of run 3 and the final candidate. Do you accept that, or should I trim it? The cheapest trim is to test H-raise-budget only at the run-2 cut, since your comment argues against it.

I'll send the routing table once these are answered.
